name: MA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Dan Koh's large fundraising advantage ($4.7M vs $0.4M)
Open seat after Moulton's retirement, but seat stays with the incumbent party
model.rationale: This Massachusetts seat carries an 11-point Democratic lean, and Koh has outraised Republican Micah Jones roughly ten-to-one with no outside spending against him. Markets price a Democratic win near 96%, consistent with fundamentals pointing to a roughly 20-point margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Koh would be the first signal that the open seat is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Seth Moulton's retirement leaves this Massachusetts district open, but the seat remains firmly on Democratic terrain with an 11-point partisan lean. Dan Koh has built a commanding financial position, raising about $4.7 million and holding nearly $2 million on hand, while Republican Micah Jones has raised under $450,000. No outside groups are spending against Koh, and prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 96% chance of holding the seat.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin of about 20 points. The main uncertainty is the usual open-seat risk, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
